Please run a cycle-1 audit on the newly-staged instance
  `films_winning_at_least_8_academy_awards` (use the pkdb-bench-audit
  skill).

  Important context: this instance went through 1 round of
  pre-staging design review by the audit agent BEFORE cycle-0
  staging. The pre-staging review issued "Revise Before Cycle-0
  Staging" verdict with 5 required fixes all applied in cycle-0:
  - Threshold ≥8 (15 rows) instead of initially-proposed ≥7 (28
    rows with more boundary churn) or ≥9 (only 7 rows below gate)
  - Master source switched from 'Academy Award records' (superlatives
    article) to 'List of Academy Award–winning films' (Film/Year/
    Awards/Nominations table)
  - Everything Everywhere All at Once (2022) corrected from 8 Oscars
    (wrong) to 7 Oscars (audit-confirmed) and excluded under ≥8
  - Director normalization uses semicolon-delim format for West Side
    Story ('Robert Wise; Jerome Robbins')
  - Best Picture Winner closed Yes/No vocab with Cabaret documented
    as calibration row

  Instance summary: 15 rows × 5 cols. aggregation-category Culture/
  Film instance chipping `aggregation` from gap 3 to gap 2 (3 of 5
  staged). claim_type = source_defined (universe = master article
  table filtered to Awards ≥ 8). source_count = 16 (1 master + 15
  per-film).

  Schema (5 cols, single PK):
  - Film (PK) — per-film Wikipedia article canonical title
  - Year of Release — integer per per-film infobox
  - Total Oscars Won — integer per master Awards column (the
    AGGREGATION cell — pre-aggregated COUNT)
  - Best Picture Winner — closed Yes/No vocab
  - Director — text per per-film infobox; semicolon-delim
    multi-director

  Pre-flagged risks for cycle-1 attention:
  1. AGGREGATION CATEGORY-FIT: Total Oscars Won is pre-aggregated by
     the master article (not computed by model from raw per-award
     rows). Mirror precedent: us_presidents_count_by_birth_state
     uses the same pattern. Audit may verify the aggregation-
     category honesty framing in source_coverage_notes.

  2. CABARET CALIBRATION CASE: Cabaret (1972, 8 Oscars) is the only
     Best Picture = 'No' row in the universe (lost Best Picture to
     The Godfather 1972). Documented as benchmark calibration cell.

  3. WEST SIDE STORY CO-DIRECTORS: 'Robert Wise; Jerome Robbins'
     semicolon-delim per per-film article co-director credit. Both
     shared the Best Director Oscar.

  4. DIACRITIC PRESERVED: 'Miloš Forman' for Amadeus per per-film
     article canonical form.

  5. EEAAO 2022 EXCLUDED: won 7 competitive Oscars not 8 (cycle-0
     correction per audit). Audit may verify this is correct count.

  6. POST-WINDOW FILMS: Oppenheimer (2023, 7 Oscars) and Gravity
     (2013, 7 Oscars) are NOT in the ≥8 universe. Future films
     would extend the universe only if they win ≥8 competitive
     Oscars (rare event).

  7. THRESHOLD CHOICE: ≥8 is curator-chosen per audit recommendation
     over ≥7 (more boundary churn) or ≥9 (below gate).

  8. SORT ORDER: Total Oscars Won desc primary + Year of Release
     asc tiebreak. Matches natural 'most-awarded films first'
     narrative.

  Per the audit skill, classify findings as BLOCKING / NON-BLOCKING
  HYGIENE / SUGGESTION. Append findings to <id>.comments.json
  (append-only). Do not edit the canonical CSV/draft/curation files.

Bundle: Full pre-registration sweep. Scope: cycle-1 audit of `films_winning_at_least_8_academy_awards` using the cited source set first, with a bounded Wiki-family source discovery pass.

Verdict: Ready, but not Ready+Clean. The CSV row universe and answer cells are source-grounded and registration-ready at the data level. Two prose/source-role hygiene issues should be cleaned up before marking this instance Ready+Clean.

Checks Passed

- Universe completeness: PASS. The cited master source `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Academy_Award%E2%80%93winning_films`, Film / Year / Awards / Nominations table, currently yields exactly 15 films with `Awards >= 8`. The staged CSV has the exact same film set: Ben-Hur, Titanic, The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King, West Side Story, Gigi, The Last Emperor, The English Patient, Gone with the Wind, From Here to Eternity, On the Waterfront, My Fair Lady, Cabaret, Gandhi, Amadeus, and Slumdog Millionaire. No missing or extra rows were found.
- Threshold exclusions: PASS. The same master table lists Everything Everywhere All at Once (2022) with 7 awards, Oppenheimer (2023) with 7 awards, and Gravity (2013) with 7 awards, so all are correctly excluded under the `Awards >= 8` universe rule. Evidence: staged ground-truth source `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Academy_Award%E2%80%93winning_films`, rows for Everything Everywhere All at Once, Oppenheimer, and Gravity.
- Total Oscars Won cells: PASS. All 15 staged `Total Oscars Won` values match the master table's leading competitive-awards count. `Gone with the Wind` appears as `8 (2)` in the source; staging `8` is correct because the source states competitive Oscars are separated from non-competitive awards and bracketed counts are non-competitive.
- Per-film Year and Director cells: PASS. The 15 per-film source URLs support the staged `Year of Release` and `Director` cells through infobox release-date / directed-by fields. Spot/full sweep examples: West Side Story has `Directed by Robert Wise Jerome Robbins` and release date 1961, matching `Robert Wise; Jerome Robbins`; Amadeus has `Directed by Miloš Forman` and 1984 release dates; Slumdog Millionaire has `Directed by Danny Boyle` and first release in 2008; all other staged director cells matched their per-film infoboxes.
- Best Picture Winner cells: PASS. The 14 `Yes` rows are supported by per-film pages carrying Best Picture winner evidence/category, and Cabaret is correctly staged `No`: its per-film page states it holds the record for most Oscars earned by a film not honoured for Best Picture. Evidence: staged per-film sources, especially `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabaret_(1972_film)`, lead / awards text.
- Shape and metadata: PASS. CSV is 15 rows x 5 columns; single `Film` PK is unique; `source_count = 16` equals `len(source_urls) = 16`; `query_category = aggregation`; `operation_type = aggregation`; `claim_type = source_defined`; `domain = Culture/Film` matches the domain taxonomy.
- Sort order: PASS. CSV is sorted by `Total Oscars Won` descending, then `Year of Release` ascending within ties. The 8-award tie runs 1939, 1953, 1954, 1964, 1972, 1982, 1984, 2008, as documented.
- Aggregation category-fit: PASS. The curation honestly frames `Total Oscars Won` as a source-provided pre-aggregated COUNT over competitive wins grouped by film, not as model-side computation from raw award rows. This is acceptable aggregation-category fit under current benchmark policy.
- Wiki-family discovery: PASS. The staged master source is the direct Wikipedia list/table source for this universe. The previously proposed `List of Academy Award records` page is useful for superlatives but not a more direct universe source for this table. No missing Wiki-family source was found that changes scope or row membership.

Findings

1. Current-state prose still contains stale/off-universe calibration examples and draft-note fragments. (factual, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE)
- Evidence in `draft.json::_extraction_notes`: the confidence-gradient paragraph says `Schindler's List — wait, Schindler's List won 7 not 8` and `The Best Years of Our Lives 1946 — wait this has 7 Oscars, not in universe`. These are not current staged rows and the `wait` notes read like unresolved draft commentary.
- Evidence in `curation.json::decision_log`: the candidate card says `Gone with the Wind, Schindler's List — wait Schindler's List has 7 not in universe`.
- Evidence in `curation.json::normalization_decisions`: the Director-normalization paragraph gives `Steven Spielberg` / `Schindler's List — wait Schindler's List has 7 Oscars not in universe` as an example inside the current rule text.
- Evidence in `draft.json::temporal_note`, `curation.json::decision_log`, and `curation.json::open_questions`: the text describes `Gravity` as `8th-Oscar-but-non-Best-Picture` / `8-Oscars-non-Best-Picture`, but the cited master source lists Gravity with 7 awards. Source locator: `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Academy_Award%E2%80%93winning_films`, row `Gravity | 2013 | 7 | 10`.
- Why this is not blocking: the CSV excludes Schindler's List, The Best Years of Our Lives, and Gravity correctly under the `Awards >= 8` rule. The issue is stale/inaccurate current-state prose, not answer-key data.
- Recommended repair: remove the `wait` fragments and replace off-universe examples with in-universe examples, e.g. `Gone with the Wind`, `Amadeus`, `Slumdog Millionaire`, `Gigi`, `From Here to Eternity`, and `Cabaret`. Rewrite the Gravity aside as `Gravity (2013, 7 Oscars, non-Best-Picture) is excluded under the >=8 threshold` or drop it entirely.

2. `source_coverage_notes` overstates the master source's Best Picture provenance as a column. (structural, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE)
- Evidence: `curation.json::source_coverage_notes` says the master article supplies `Best Picture Winner` status from the master article's `Best-Picture-winner column`. The cited master table has visible columns `Film`, `Year`, `Awards`, and `Nominations`; the page-level prose says Best Picture winners are indicated by styling (shaded/bold), not by a parsed Best Picture column. Source locator: `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Academy_Award%E2%80%93winning_films`, article lead and Film / Year / Awards / Nominations table.
- Why this is not blocking: the staged `Best Picture Winner` cells are still source-grounded by the per-film pages and by the master page's Best-Picture styling convention. The problem is the word `column`, which misdescribes the source structure.
- Recommended repair: change the role text to say Best Picture status is verified from the master page's Best-Picture styling convention plus per-film article cross-checks, not from a dedicated master-table column.

Counts

Issue-type counts: 1 factual, 1 structural, 0 scope-related.
